name: Great Hafir inlet
summary: An 85-metre dug inlet channel with paired earthworks that guided runoff into the Great Hafir reservoir at Musawwarat es-Sufra.
description: A roughly 85-metre excavated inlet channel and paired earthworks leading into the Great Hafir basin.
tier_reason: An inlet can be fine detail; it is a separate hydraulic role, not a duplicate reservoir. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.label: by c. 350 CE (inferred)
date.basis: The excavated inlet belongs to the water-collection configuration described for the Great Hafir; individual inlet commissioning is undated.

events.statement: The excavated inlet and earthworks are interpreted as having directed runoff into the Great Hafir reservoir.
events.population: The Kushite Musawwarat religious-site water users and maintainers
events.caveats: The Great Hafir’s construction is radiocarbon-constrained to the 6th–4th centuries BCE; neither its original commissioning nor the ducts’ precise age is individually dated. The 350 CE endpoint is only a broad Meroitic contextual estimate, not a hard archaeological cutoff.

evidence.supports: The project describes the reservoir, 85 m inlet and water ducts supplying the Great Enclosure in its Meroitic context.
Dates the Great Hafir construction horizon and provides the Meroitic regional context.
